units: pixels (x right, y down) and seconds; no metric scale
background: uniform flat grey (RGB ~78,79,86, std 0.2), no ground, horizon, markings or other static objects

camera.motion: static (background identical in all frames; no pan/shake)
camera.perspective: side view; both objects move horizontally in planes facing the camera. Apparent lengths change slightly with image x (end faces visible off-axis): airliner 857 px near image centre/left to 876 px at x~1470; car 128 px at x~1000 to 137 px at both edges. Vertical sizes constant. The airliner and car are probably at different depths (unknown); the single-scale 2D convention would use the prior object's own pixel size/speed.

airliner.description: large white Air China passenger jet (red phoenix logo on tail fin, 'AIR CHINA' on fuselage, reg. B-9918), side view, nose pointing left; upper object
airliner.ref_point: bbox centre (x0+x1)/2, (y0+y1)/2 when fully visible; when cut by the frame edge, visible far edge -/+ (full length-1)/2 (column ref_source)
airliner.per_frame_step_px: nose (leading edge) moves 57.0 px/frame from frame 1->2 to the end, constant; bbox-centre steps 56-59 px (perspective length change), mean 57.53 over frames 12-30

car.description: small white/silver angular pickup (Cybertruck-like), side view, front pointing left; lower object, below the airliner
car.ref_point: bbox centre; edge-based estimate when cut by the frame edge
car.per_frame_step_px: 28.45 px/frame constant (leading edge and centre), from frame 1->2 to the end

events.event: both objects stationary between frame 0 and frame 1 (identical positions); motion starts at frame 1 (first displacement frame 1->2)

interactions: none: no contact, no bounce, no direction change, no image overlap. At the start the car is below the airliner's fuselage span; the faster airliner pulls ahead and its tail tip (bbox x1) passes the car's front (bbox x0) between frame 24 (1206 vs 1186) and frame 25 (1149 vs 1158).
horizontal_gap_ref_points: airliner and car origins: see tracks; e.g. frame 24 dx = 473 px, dy = 225.5 px
